Two features of the cordless sweeper made by Hollingsworth Home Products were altered after the company's first home trial cycle closed in March.
The dust container on the sample unit was enlarged, and the power switch was moved from the body of the machine to the handle. Comments about the noise of the motor were also common, but the motor itself was left unchanged.
Ninety households took part, each using a preproduction unit for six weeks in place of its own cleaning equipment and filing three short written reports.
"A machine behaves differently in a home than it does in our testing rooms," said Nigel Braithwaite, who manages the panel program at the research office. "Neither change would have been made without the panel."
The cycle now under way differs in one respect. Members are being placed in two groups, and one group will keep its sample unit for twelve weeks instead of six.
Gwen Aldridge, contributing writer, Household Trade Review

Display Windows for Local Makers
Who takes part
The program borrows shop windows that stand empty between tenants and fills them with work by makers based in the town. The categories change each season. Last season's round covered hand-bound books and woven baskets. This season the program is open to makers working in clay, glass, wood, or textiles.
How sites are allocated
Sites are grouped by window size, and makers who submit larger work are offered the wider windows. Each allocated site comes with one loaned fixture, listed in the site directory. The fixture stays in the window for the season and is returned to the office when the display closes.
Before you install
Every maker must attend one briefing session before any work is placed in a window. Makers holding Zone A sites attend on 6 March at Larkfield Market House. Makers holding Zone B sites attend on 8 March at Oxley Community Hall. Start times are sent by e-mail. Bring your allocation notice with you.
